I've updated the code to use default values when timestamps are not found or when there's an error:

1. When no start date is found, `start_timestamp` will be set to 0 (Unix epoch)
2. When no end date is found, `end_timestamp` will be set to the current timestamp
3. If there's any error during parsing, the method will return the same default values (0 for start and current time for end)

These changes ensure the code always returns valid timestamp values rather than `None`, which matches your requirements.
